model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of Mistralv0.2-Base when fine-tuned on six medical specialties—Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics—evaluated against per-specialty terms. The vertical axis represents “Negative log probability,” ranging from -22 to -27 with tick marks at integer intervals, where lower values indicate better model performance. The horizontal axis lists the six specialties as categories, each containing a group of six bars corresponding to the model’s performance when fine-tuned on each specialty (as indicated by the legend: light blue for Cardio, light orange for Gastro, medium orange for Infect, dark orange for Neuro, brown for Obstetrics, and dark brown for Pediatrics). Within each group, the bars are arranged in the same order as the legend, and their heights reflect the negative log probability for that fine-tuning condition on the respective specialty’s terms. For example, in the “Cardio” group, the light blue bar (fine-tuned on Cardio) is the shortest (best performance, ~-26.8), while the dark brown bar (fine-tuned on Pediatrics) is the tallest (worst performance, ~-22.5). A consistent pattern emerges: each specialty’s own fine-tuned model performs best (lowest negative log probability) on its own terms, while performance degrades when evaluated on terms from other specialties, particularly those more distant in medical domain. The chart visually emphasizes this specialization effect through the descending bar heights within each group, with the self-fine-tuned bar consistently at the bottom.
